title: Motor Transport Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
1.     MOS 3510, Motor Transport Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Motor Transport Officer plans, coordinates, executes
and supervises the execution of all functions of motor transport. Motor
Transport Officers analyze, translate, and execute commander’s operational
requirements and intent to support mission requirements at the battalion,
squadron, regiment, MSC, MEF and HQMC levels. As a motor transport subject
matter expert, Motor Transport Officers are responsible for: planning,
executing, and monitoring tactical wheeled vehicle movements, planning and
forecasting of equipment readiness and availability, monitoring and managing
motor transport maintenance requirements, advising commanders on motor
transport maintenance and operations requirements, management of individual
and collective motor transport training, and management of motor transport
licensing programs. Due to the complex technical nature of motor transport,
years of experience and training are required to become proficient.
Depending on the unit and grade, Motor Transport Officers can be assigned as
a Special Staff Officer, a Motor Transport Platoon Commander, a Motor
Transport Maintenance Officer or a combination of all three.

       b.    Prerequisites

        (1) Warrant Officers assigned to this MOS must have previously served
in one of the following motor transport related MOSs 3521, 3529, 3531, or
3537.

        (2) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

       c.    Requirements

        (1) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

        (2) Complete the Motor Transport Maintenance Officers Course (MTMOC)
(M03MBJ7), Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.    Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) First-Line Supervisors of Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle
Operators 53-1043.

             (2) First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
49-1011.

       f.    Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
